Article: Review, sign off, and annotate incoming lab results
Physicians can review, annotate, and sign off on incoming diagnostics efficiently by following the steps below. Only users with clinical provider roles may sign results.

1. Navigate to **Clinical > Lab Queue**.
2. Select the pending result from the unreviewed list to open the viewer.
3. Type any necessary clinical notes into the **Annotations** text box.
4. To route an abnormal finding to a covering physician, click **Delegate**, select the covering provider from the dropdown, and click **Send**.
5. Click **Sign Off** to finalize the review and automatically file the report into the patient chart.

**Limits & Conditions**
Results marked critical cannot be signed off without an added annotation. Delegated results remain locked for the original ordering physician until the covering provider completes the review.

**Troubleshooting**
If the **Sign Off** button appears grayed out, verify that all mandatory annotation fields are complete. If a covering provider does not appear in the delegation list, check **Settings > Staff** to ensure their active coverage schedule is correctly configured.

Ticket:
Inquiry regarding routing and annotating incoming lab results

Good afternoon, I am terribly sorry to drop this into your queue, but I wanted to make sure I am handling incoming diagnostic reports correctly in the system. When I review and annotate incoming lab results from our local hospital network, is there a specific way to route abnormal values to a covering physician if the primary provider is out of the office? I tried looking through the filing menu earlier today, but I got a bit lost and didn't want to misplace any critical patient data.

In the meantime, you can follow these steps to route abnormal values to a covering physician:
1. Navigate to **Clinical > Lab Queue**.
2. Select the pending result from the unreviewed list to open the viewer.
3. Enter any necessary clinical notes in the **Annotations** text box.
4. Click **Delegate**, choose the covering provider from the dropdown, and click **Send** to route the abnormal finding.
5. Once the covering provider has reviewed the result, click **Sign Off** to finalize the review and file the report into the patient chart.

Please note that only users with clinical provider roles may sign off on results, and critical results require an added annotation before they can be signed off. If you encounter any issues, such as the **Sign Off** button being grayed out, ensure all mandatory annotation fields are completed.

If you have any further questions or need additional assistance, feel free to let us know."
